seams.oldContract: Custom scripts staged a Node Host/runtime descriptor and signed one macOS app.
seams.newContract: Primary runtime bundles pinned Node/Python/pnpm with payload hashes, update qualification, signing, and mandatory policy metadata.
seams.breakage: Old package/install scripts would bypass the new runtime and release closure.
seams.migration: Extend current packaging inputs; do not replay the old staging implementation.

seams.oldContract: desktop-custom-composition patched the then-current base/web Cordis graph.
seams.newContract: The package/module graph and generated catalogs have expanded and changed ownership.
seams.breakage: Old patch entries can reference removed packages or duplicate new native services.

seams.oldContract: Custom client packages were loaded through the old export/slot conventions.
seams.newContract: Generated client catalogs, module packages, scoped slots, factory slots, and dockkit drive loading.

seams.oldContract: desktop-custom isolated profile/userData while approved settings and sessions were shared.
seams.newContract: Desktop and Host default to desktop; profile resolution, primary runtime installation, and automatic session migrations are new.
seams.breakage: An unqualified launch could use the official profile or migrate shared stores under unreviewed assumptions.

seams.oldContract: Run projection consumed older agent/session/tool/retry events with custom attempt correlation.
seams.newContract: Turn/step lifecycle, LlmAttemptId, compact assistant streams, durable retry waterfall, and structured terminal reasons are canonical.
seams.breakage: The old projection would misinterpret or miss new events and cannot invent RunId semantics.
seams.migration: Define an explicit new-event-to-RunId projection adapter and replay fixtures before integrating policy.

seams.oldContract: Custom policy observed provider errors, request attempts, reasoning, usage, and streams through older hooks.
seams.newContract: LlmFailure, LlmAttemptId, reasoningEffort capabilities, disjoint usage fields, transient streams, and provider-owned retry are explicit.
seams.breakage: Old error/retry and reasoning adapters would duplicate or conflict with provider behavior.

seams.oldContract: Custom durable events/projections targeted the older Session envelope.
seams.newContract: Session format v3, static migrations, generation/lease verification, known-event catalog, and ignorable unknown-event rules apply.
seams.breakage: Directly writing old custom envelopes can be rejected or make cross-version persistence unsafe.
seams.migration: Design TaskCheckpoint/Run durable facts for v3 and register or safely mark extension events according to upstream rules.

seams.oldContract: Custom pressure policy and compaction modified the old compaction-basic flow.
seams.newContract: Upstream owns token thresholds, atomic brackets, replacement generations, pruning, offload, and overflow recovery.
seams.breakage: Replaying the old engine would create two compaction systems and discard new safety behavior.
seams.migration: Keep upstream executor; add thin task-aware eligibility, low/medium scope, and deterministic fact validation.

seams.oldContract: A custom remote exposed Run State to RunStatusDock and closed the idle composer gap.
seams.newContract: Session controller transport, generated client APIs, scoped modules, and dockkit own current UI composition.

strategy.name: Fresh latest-upstream branch plus semantic capability port
strategy.rationale: All eleven registered seams changed, the histories diverge by 1548 upstream commits versus 12 baseline-only commits, and upstream now natively owns several foundations that old patches would duplicate.

rejected.A: Rebase would replay obsolete implementation assumptions across every changed seam and make conflict resolution look like semantic validation.
rejected.C: Full or broad cherry-pick preserves historical file-level patches rather than current capability contracts; only isolated commits may later be mined as evidence.
rejected.D: A hybrid integration strategy obscures the single source of truth. Selective source reuse is allowed inside strategy B, but the branch and architecture remain latest-upstream-first.

portOrder.goal: Run State, backend health, and error classification
tests: RunId is a pure function of the durable turn
no live open turn yields no active run
backend observation never becomes run authority
portOrder.stopGate: Unknown is guessed, fatal evidence is weak, or terminal state can regress.
decisions: D7.1 run authority is one durable upstream turn keyed by SessionId and turn, not agent-process lifetime, a task, an LlmAttemptId, or a RetryId
D7.2 RunId is deterministic and injective over SessionId and turn, with no random, process-local, or counter allocation and no new Session event
D7.3 an active run exists only while a live turn is open, and no live open turn means no active run
D7.4 terminal reasons are preserved as recorded, and interrupted is after-the-fact repair closure rather than a live failure
D7.5 a retry never allocates a second run and stays inside the same RunId, turn, and step
D7.6 Stage 7 publishes no durable AttemptId and never persists, derives, or reads LlmAttemptId
D7.7 the package is a pure library with no second Agent Loop, no second Session persistence, and no new Session events
D7.8 the run projection is derived from the normalized Stage 6 agent-lifecycle-facts input
D7.9 backend observation is a separate diagnostic dimension that never derives a RunId
D7.10 Unknown stays Unknown at every level and no backend state is fabricated
D7.11 only a backend-neutral observation contract is implemented, because the current source exposes no diagnostics seam to adapt
D7.12 fatal classification requires strong structured evidence and message text is never classified
D7.13 a cancellation is a durable terminal outcome and stays degraded even when a stronger signal carried it
D7.14 error precedence is deterministic, total, and arrival-order independent: terminal, then execution, then client, then observer, then earliest time
D7.15 a terminal run is retained as history and never stays active after turn/end
D7.16 no new required Session event type is introduced

portOrder.goal: TaskCheckpoint, Result Manifest, and guarded resume
tests: result manifest ordering and revision monotonicity
post-turn-start Run adoption on a live Session
legacy required event compatibility through restore
portOrder.stopGate: Authoritative task facts can be lost or duplicated.
decisions: D8.1 TaskCheckpoint is the task authority and the Stage 7 Run State stays the execution authority; neither derives the other and no task fact ever mints a Run
D8.2 originRunId is the immutable first Run, only latestRunId advances, and it advances only after an actual durable turn/start committed
D8.3 no RunId is pre-allocated and no future turn is predicted: the caller passes a turn, the producer mints runIdFor(sessionId, turn), and only a turn already committed is accepted
D8.4 resumeRecord.runId is the RunId of the turn that actually started, never the Run the resume was expected to use
D8.5 every new task/checkpoint and task/result-manifest write travels the typed ignorable append seam, and a pre-seam event without the marker stays valid and is never rewritten

D8.6 checkpoint revisions are monotonic per Task: no predecessor yields revision 1, revision N plus a successor yields N+1, a stale expected revision fails closed, an equal revision is rejected, and a regression is rejected
D8.7 two competing successors of one predecessor cannot both become authoritative, because the second observes a stale expected revision and fails closed
D8.8 a ResultManifest is a separate monotonic document and a checkpoint citing revision N is only accepted once revision N is durably appended, so no forward reference exists
D8.9 the task step partition is coherent: completed, current, and pending are mutually exclusive and a resume plan never contains a completed step

D8.10 guarded resume returns a structured policy result rather than a boolean, with classes allowed, requires_confirmation, blocked, and not_applicable carrying a reason code, taskId, checkpoint revision, latest and durable run, step ids, and hazard evidence
D8.11 no checkpoint is not_applicable, a completed or cancelled Task is not resumable, and a blocked or fatally failed Task is decided before any hazard reclassification
D8.12 TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN is a hard hazard that requires confirmation, while TOOL_NOT_STARTED is not by itself blocking
D8.13 a running Task interrupted with no hazard resumes as allowed with a pending-only plan
D8.14 the durable Run of the Session must equal the checkpoint latestRunId; divergence fails closed to require confirmation instead of reinterpreting the log
D8.15 completed-step evidence is validated before resume: a tool-result citation must match a durably successful result and a result-validation citation must name a durably passed manifest revision
D8.16 the resume context is bounded by the Stage 6 contract and omits historical reasoning, the full session log, and raw tool output explicitly rather than trimming silently
D8.17 the started Run is adopted outside the active append publication stack: the seam observes the committed turn/start and defers the write, because a Session observer may not reenter append
D8.18 the producers are the single writer of task facts; no second persistence path, sidecar, SQLite table, raw JSONL writer, or independent sequence exists
D8.19 backend health is not a resume requirement and no backend state participates in the decision
D8.20 Stage 7 authority is unchanged: Stage 8 consumes runIdFor as a pure derivation and adds no Run event, Run format, or allocation
D8.21 the Stage 8 prerequisite was the typed ignorable append seam landed separately in commit 5262a0cabb, and Stage 8 itself adds no new Session event type

portOrder.goal: IQ3_S reasoning and bounded run policy
tests: reasoning resolution matrix over the real LlmRuntime prepareCall seam
requested and resolved reasoning stay distinct
unsupported effort never becomes a request
initial attempt plus two retries is the maximum automatic chain
fatal, cancellation, and no-retry categories never retry
retry stays in one turn, step, and RunId
portOrder.stopGate: A second retry engine appears or request reasoning cannot be proven.
decisions: D9.1 requested reasoning and resolved reasoning are distinct facts and a resolution never reports a level as resolved merely because it was requested

D9.2 reasoning capability is read from the current upstream adapter contract, so no second capability database, no repository-owned reasoning level enum, and no host, model, or file path is hard-coded
D9.3 an unsupported effort is a terminal policy outcome: nothing is dropped, promoted, or substituted and no request is formed
D9.4 an invalid configuration fails closed at the policy boundary, so correctness never depends on a backend rejecting the request
D9.5 a capability whose declared default is not among its advertised efforts is incoherent configuration and fails closed rather than being rounded into a resolution
D9.6 the retry policy governs the existing llm-retry executor through one outermost agent/request-error listener and replaces no executor, adapter policy, backoff, retry identity, or durable event

D9.7 the hard ceiling is two automatic retries after the initial attempt, which is three attempts; the cap counts retries and never attempts, and a deployment configuration may lower it but never raise it

D9.8 fatal categories, cancellation, a blocked run, a closed turn, a tool-semantics failure, a generation stall, a reached max-token limit, an invalid model or reasoning configuration, a context overflow Stage 10 owns, and a failed retry chain are denied even when the captured provider policy would retry them
D9.9 retryability is read from the captured provider policy and the Stage 7 category, message text is never classified, and a failure no current contract names is denied rather than assumed transient
D9.10 the retry budget is folded from committed llm/retry events into a Session projection, so the count is durable rather than a process-local counter and survives a restart
D9.11 a permitted retry stays inside the same Session, turn, RunId, and step; the policy opens no Run, advances no checkpoint, records no resume, and adds no Session event type
D9.12 guarded resume is never invoked by the retry policy, and a Session interruption or a fatal category is denied rather than converted into a continuation
D9.13 backend health is not a retry input: no reachability observation, backend state, or health adapter participates in the decision
D9.14 Stage 7 Run authority and Stage 8 guarded resume are unchanged, and Stage 9 predicts no future turn and allocates no RunId
D9.15 the reasoning policy is a library with no plugin entry while the retry policy is a plugin whose configuration is validated before any listener is installed

portOrder.stopGate: Compaction can mutate checkpoints, delete evidence, or lower main reasoning.
decisions: D10.1 the basic compaction engine remains the only compaction executor; Stage 10 adds no second engine, writer, lock, retry authority, Session event type, or generic blob evidence library

D10.2 the candidate policy is a minimal optional seam (assess, begin, and a transaction exposing decorateRequest, validateCandidate, rebaseAfterOwnedRecovery, assertPublishable, and audit) and a context with no policy mounted takes exactly the path it took before the seam existed

D10.3 no durable authority is deleted or rewritten; only the model-visible Session surface and its derived messages change, and the protection block is derived from the append-only log that keeps every original event

D10.4 the protection root is canonically serialized and digest-hashed, and the published replacement carries exactly that canonical value between its delimiters, so deterministic re-validation fails a reordered list, a duplicated block, or an edited fact

D10.5 the published protection block is code-rendered through the decoration replacement content and appended verbatim after the model narrative, so the narrative can never author or edit the block it would have to reproduce

D10.6 assertPublishable is synchronous by contract and runs in the same uninterrupted block that appends the replacement, so a checkpoint revision, a referenced result revision, an evidence identity, a hazard set, or a main-Run reasoning change during summarization stops publication instead of being papered over

D10.7 a Session that tracks no Task is fail-open: it admits every entry, opens an inert transaction that decorates nothing and accepts the executor own candidate, and reports an audit without a protection digest

D10.8 the auxiliary reasoning ladder is exactly low then medium, and the first rung must be advertisable on the executor own declared route or the compaction fails closed before any auxiliary model call

D10.9 maxSummaryValidationRetries defaults to 0, keeping the upstream single-candidate behavior byte-identical, and the DS desktop layer sets exactly 1, which is one further candidate and never a third
D10.10 CONTEXT_OVERFLOW is routed to compaction recovery rather than retry, because recovering a context overflow is a compaction decision and Stage 9 deliberately left it to Stage 10
D10.11 no new Session event type is introduced; compaction/summary gains an optional backward-compatible audit field that a reader predating Stage 10 ignores

D10.12 the desktop-custom bundle is a tail Cordis patch layer after base and web-app that registers the task checkpoint, run policy, and task-aware compaction policy rows and restates the compaction executor with one further candidate
D10.13 the retired package-set custom composition, its patch reload path, and the old composition metadata stay rejected: the new layer appends to the upstream prefix and never rewrites it
D10.14 admission runs before any destructive model-context operation, so a refusal never leaves the surface already pruned or truncated

D10.15 the policy appends no Session event, writes no projection, creates no lock, retries nothing, and deletes nothing; its only durable trace is the optional audit field on the executor own summary event

D10.16 capacity is consulted only when the route advertises a window, and an unpriced route means the policy makes no capacity claim, so the executor own capacity error stays the owner of that failure mode

safety.dataPlan: Use temporary DSH_HOME/userData/profile roots and copied synthetic/released fixtures only. Never point the adaptation build or migration code at the user's settings, sessions, profiles, or Application Support.
safety.nativePlan: Adopt the upstream primary-runtime lock, then verify architecture, payload hashes, codesign, Node/Python execution, native/system, node-pty, koffi, sharp, Host startup, and renderer loading in an isolated candidate.

compatibilityDebt.reason: Stage 6 restored the two Final Product task events as first-party known v3 events and shipped the durable task-checkpoint contract plus a read-only lifecycle fact extractor, but Run State, retained capability ports, guarded resume, and a new product baseline remain unresolved.

knownUnknowns: Formal Developer ID/notarization and daily installation remain intentionally outside the isolated Stage 4 candidate qualification.
Stage 7 fixed the turn-scoped RunId contract, so the remaining Run State unknown is only whether a live consumer may cache that projection instead of recomputing it; that is a Stage 11 question.

Stage 7 shipped the backend observation contract but no adapter, because the current source exposes no backend health or status seam to read; a later stage must add or find one before a local GGUF backend can report more than unknown.
Whether guarded and pending-only resume may proceed without a durable attempt identity, given that Stage 6 kept LlmAttemptId transient and non-durable, is a Stage 8 question.

Stage 9 resolved the IQ3_S route mapping by resolving against the adapter-published LlmResolvedModelInfo.reasoning instead of a repository-owned catalog, so capability is proven from the adapter contract without reading real settings and no host path, model id, or reasoning level is hard-coded.
The current dockkit/scoped-slot insertion contract for Run Details needs a minimal renderer prototype after its remote contract stabilizes.
Retained capability ports and current-client qualification remain unproven until their later stages.
